question: A Project's knowledge base has grown until it approaches the limit of what fits in the context window. Which two statements are accurate? Select two.
options: A) The Project stays in retrieval mode permanently, even if its knowledge is reduced later.
B) The user has to switch retrieval on in the settings once the knowledge passes that threshold.
C) Claude switches over to retrieval automatically, with no configuration needed from the user.
D) Retrieval disables web search and the other features for every chat inside that Project.
E) Retrieval lets the Project work with roughly ten times more content than it held before.
correct_answers: C) Claude switches over to retrieval automatically, with no configuration needed from the user.
E) Retrieval lets the Project work with roughly ten times more content than it held before.
explanations: Incorrect. The Project reverts to standard processing if the knowledge later drops back below the threshold.
Incorrect. There is no setting to turn on; treating it as manual is the most common misunderstanding of this behaviour.
Correct. Retrieval mode for Projects turns on by itself as the knowledge approaches the limit; there is nothing to configure.
Incorrect. Retrieval works alongside other Claude features, including web search, extended thinking and Research.
Correct. In retrieval mode a Project can hold up to about ten times more content than standard processing allows.
